name: Cape Verde
title: Holidays in Cape Verde
intro: Year-round sunshine, wide sandy beaches and lemon sharks in the shallows off West Africa. Here's what Cape Verde is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: You register online before you travel and pay an airport fee. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Cape Verde is warm and sunny all year, which makes it popular for winter sun. December to February can be very windy, which suits kitesurfers more than young children. Late summer is hottest and most humid, and September can bring short tropical downpours. Euros are widely accepted.

things.name: Santa Maria beach
things.blurb: A long sandy beach with shallow areas, beach bars and a busy pier where fishermen land their catch.

things.name: Pedra de Lume salt crater
things.blurb: Float in super-salty pools inside an old volcanic crater.

things.name: Shark Bay
things.blurb: Wade into warm, shallow water to watch young lemon sharks swim around your legs.

things.name: Buracona Blue Eye
things.blurb: Natural rock pools by the sea and a cave where sunlight turns the water bright blue.

things.name: Turtle watching
things.blurb: Guided night walks from July to October to see loggerhead turtles nesting.

things.name: Kitesurf and windsurf lessons
things.blurb: Lessons on Kite Beach for older children and teens when the wind is right.

faqs.question: Is Cape Verde good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, for easy beach holidays with guaranteed sun. Sal and Boa Vista have big all-inclusive resorts with pools and kids' clubs. There is less to do away from the beach than in the Canaries.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: A week is right for most families. Ten days allows time for an island hop or more day trips.

faqs.question: How do you get there from the UK?
faqs.answer: There are direct flights to Sal and Boa Vista from several UK airports, about six hours. British passport holders don't need a visa but must register online and pay an airport fee before travel.

faqs.question: Is the sea safe for swimming?
faqs.answer: Santa Maria bay on Sal is usually calm. Other beaches can have strong waves and currents, so swim near lifeguards or in the hotel pool on windy days.
